summary:
Vert (vert.nyc; vertventures.io now redirects there) runs its portfolio through three publishing entities and three App Store developer accounts. Together these hold exactly 8 iOS apps, which matches the site's "8 Apps" claim:
(1) "Vert Ventures" (seller Vert Ventures LLC, Apple artist id 1719671063) publishes Astra - Life Advice.
(2) "Vert Media Partners LLC" (artist id 1690446849) publishes Plug AI: Texting Assistant, formerly RizzGPT and then Wingman.
(3) "W185 Holdings" (seller W185 Holdings LLC, artist id 1761597813) publishes Strum - Play Guitar, Berry - Wellness, Saga - Stories, Sensa - ASMR, Indigo - Scan & Collect and Eagle - Swing Analysis.
The proof that W185 belongs to Vert: Google Play developer "Vert Media Partners" (contact@vertmedia.io) publishes package com.w185holdings.strum next to com.vertmedia.astra and com.vertmedia.wingman. Vert Ventures LLC's NY filing address is 185 Wythe Ave, Brooklyn, so "W185" almost certainly stands for that address (an inference). Only the three winners (Astra, Plug AI, Strum) are on Android. The 5 smaller apps exist only on iOS.

Revenue mostly comes from three apps.
- Astra (AI astrology and life-advice chat, launched 2024-01-09): about 39.3K US ratings and an estimated 56.8K worldwide. Third-party estimates put it at about $400-450K a month. It uses a hard paywall with a 7-day trial and a weekly plan (about $6.99/wk).
- Strum (AI chord recognition for any song, launched 2025-08-06, first called "Autochord"): about 20K US ratings, ranked #53 in Music, Android 500K+ downloads with 55K ratings. ScreensDesign estimates about $250K a month. Pricing is a trial then $6.99/week, or $49.99/yr with a 7-day trial.
- Plug AI (AI dating-text reply generator from screenshots, launched 2023-06-30): 15.8K US ratings, Android 1M+ downloads. Founders' podcast claims: 1.2M downloads in under 3 months and $190K a month in January 2024, and the app was listed for sale at $3.5M. Its iOS build has not been updated since 2024-08-02.
The smaller apps all use the same $6.99 subscription template:
- Berry: cycle-syncing wellness journal, 1.3K ratings, last updated February 2025.
- Saga: AI stories, 159 ratings.
- Sensa: ASMR app with 0 ratings; its description is copied from Saga, and it was dropped after 3 weeks.
- Indigo: Pokémon-style trading-card scanner (bundle "pokemonapp"), 0 ratings, March 2026.
- Eagle: AI golf swing analysis, 127 ratings, launched 2026-08-04 and actively updated.
These look like fast tests: launch quickly, then abandon or keep iterating.

People and entities:
- Co-founders, per RocketReach: Evan Dray, Alex Leiman and Will Olson. Will Olson says on LinkedIn that he joined for $250/week and became a cofounder after 6 months, and that they have reached 12M downloads and more than $30M ARR. Other staff: Alex Wang (Product & Design), Saarthak Chaturvedi (Founding SWE), Kai Mitchell (Growth), Maggie Jin (Marketing), Blaise Siefer and Dylan Kenny (Marketing Associates), Maxine San Diego (Influencer Marketing Manager).
- Vert Media Partners LLC is a California LLC (entity number reported as 202251112388), described as digital advertising, at 876 La Para Ave, Palo Alto. Its 12/13/2023 Statement of Information lists Alex Leiman, Evan Dray and Blake Anderson as managers. Blake Anderson later built Umax and Cal AI; his current role at Vert is unknown. I read this from search-engine snippets because the CA SOS site blocked direct fetching.
- Vert Ventures LLC was formed in Wyoming on 11/08/2023 and registered in NY on 6/11/2024 (doc 7367252) at 185 Wythe Ave, Brooklyn.
- The legal terms of both Vert Ventures LLC and W185 Holdings LLC say they are Wyoming LLCs. Those terms are hosted on free GitHub Pages sites under throwaway per-app accounts (consequentlyjubilant, strum-app, eagle-golf, indigo-app-1). Each app has its own Gmail support address (astracontact111@, strumappcontact@, eagleappcontact@, indigoappcontact@, contact185holdings@).

Growth timeline (all self-reported):
- September 2024 Dribbble job post: 4M users, $8M annual revenue, 8 FTE, all apps use AI.
- About October 2025, a LinkedIn recruiter post reposted by Vert: "$30M+ ARR".
- January 16, 2026, Get on Board posting: "scale apps to go viral through influencer marketing" with "250+ active partnerships across multiple apps".
- vert.nyc today: 15M+ users, $25M+ annual revenue, $0 funding, 2 years old, 23-person team. A gallery caption reads "20m ARR but ramen still hits".
These numbers do not fully agree ($25M vs $30M), and the third-party revenue estimates for the top 3 apps add up to only about $0.9M a month (about $11M a year). Treat all revenue figures as unverified.

Culture, from the site's job copy: "if we aren't shipping bugs to production, we aren't moving fast enough". Designers are told to "iterate based on A/B test results" and to favor "bias for action (read: testing and iteration) over analysis (read: case studies and user research)". The site also says "We rely heavily on AI for development". The stack is Python/JS/React/React Native/Swift. A Marketing Associate is paid $80-200K plus equity, and the ad says "no experience necessary" and asks for people who "understand culture."

How they grow (secondary sources): seeding TikTok with micro-creators (about $50 a post), faceless TikTok/YouTube accounts, and TikTok slideshows of 18-34 slides with the app shown around slides 8-10. Paywalls were tested with Superwall. Apps get renamed when needed (RizzGPT→Wingman→Plug AI, apparently after a name dispute).

implications_for_automation: Copy Vert's legal structure: a holding LLC plus several publisher LLCs and Apple developer accounts (Vert Ventures, Vert Media Partners, W185 Holdings). This spreads App Store review and ban risk (guideline 4.3 spam, 5.6 developer code of conduct) and keeps winners apart from experiments. The automated system needs an entity/account registry that maps each app to its LLC, developer account, support inbox, legal-page host and payment account.

Two-tier launch pipeline: test on iOS only (5 of 8 Vert apps never reached Android). Port to Android only after an app passes a revenue or retention threshold (Astra, Plug AI and Strum all got Android versions under a single Play account).

Use one default monetization template and A/B test from it. Every Vert app uses a free-trial hard paywall at the end of onboarding: $6.99/week, an annual anchor of $49.99-$79.99, and a $0.99 or 'limited offer' variant. Make the paywall config-driven (Superwall or RevenueCat style) so price, trial length and layout can be tested without a new build.

Long personalized onboarding is a feature, not a bug. Astra uses about 9 steps; Strum uses about 16, with a playable intro, quiz, music-service connect, permission priming, testimonials, then the paywall. This matches Bier's 'long sign up flows are fine'. Generate onboarding flows from a reusable template: goal quiz, then personalization inputs, then a 'personalizing...' interstitial, then social proof, then the paywall.

Product choice follows Bier's 'core needs' filter and favors 'AI wrapper with one magic input': screenshot to dating reply (love), birth data to astrology advice (love and self), song link to chords (play), swing video to coaching (play), card photo to market value (money and collecting). The ideation module should score ideas on (a) core need, (b) one-shot AI 'wow' within 60 seconds, (c) a visually demonstrable output for short-form video, and (d) price tolerance of at least $6.99/week.

Distribution is the moat. Vert runs 250+ concurrent influencer partnerships and has a remote influencer-ops manager who handles creator outreach, script review and video-performance logging. Earlier Plug AI growth came from $50-per-post micro-creators, faceless TikTok/YouTube accounts and 18-34-slide TikTok slideshows. An autonomous system needs: (1) creator discovery and outreach CRM, (2) script and hook generation, (3) draft review, (4) per-video performance logging tied to install attribution, (5) automated payouts, (6) owned faceless slideshow accounts in several languages. This is Bier's 'reproducible testing process', run on content instead of features.

Kill fast, but recognize winners: Sensa had 0 ratings and copied metadata and was dropped after about 3 weeks; Indigo has 0 ratings; Berry and Saga stalled. Automate kill/scale decisions with set thresholds (installs per creator post, trial start rate, trial-to-paid rate, D7 retention) so tests give clear answers, not 'maybe we needed more downloads'.

Avoid Vert's sloppiness that automation would multiply: copy-pasted descriptions (Sensa reuses Saga's text), dead Wix legal URLs still linked from store listings (vertmedia.io/terms, vertventures.io/terms) and bundle-id leftovers (com.vertventures.stella for Astra; com.w185holdings.pokemonapp, which may raise trademark issues). Add automated metadata uniqueness checks, legal-URL health checks and trademark screening, because App Review rejects spam or duplicate metadata and broken privacy URLs.

Build in a rename and rebrand path: Plug AI went RizzGPT, then Wingman, then Plug AI (apparently after a name conflict), and Strum started as 'Autochord'. Keep the app's brand layer (name, icon, store copy, landing page) separate from the codebase so a rename does not need a rebuild.

Cheap, disposable per-app infrastructure is enough: GitHub Pages legal docs generated from a Termly-style template naming the LLC (Wyoming), a per-app Gmail support inbox and a one-page static landing site. All of this can be automated through APIs (GitHub Pages, DNS registrar, Google Workspace/Gmail or a transactional email inbox, App Store Connect API, Google Play Developer API).

Expect self-reported metrics to run ahead of third-party estimates. Vert claims $25-30M ARR, while modeled estimates for its top 3 apps add up to about $11M a year. The system's own dashboard should use store-reported proceeds (App Store Connect/Play financial reports or RevenueCat), not tracker estimates.
open_questions: What is the real revenue split across apps? Third-party estimates (Astra about $400-450K/mo, Strum about $250K/mo, Plug AI about $200K/mo as of 2025) total far less than the claimed $25-30M ARR. Does the gap come from non-US revenue, Android, gross vs net, or apps not found?

Are there other Vert apps under developer accounts or LLC names not found here (for example, removed tests or the 'Plug AI: Pick Up Lines & Rizz' id6449148120 listing, now 404)? Does '8 apps' count iOS and Android separately?
What is Blake Anderson's current relationship with Vert? He is listed as a manager of Vert Media Partners LLC in the 12/13/2023 filing, but his later companies (Umax, Cal AI) are separate.
Who is Will (will@vertventures.io)? Presumably co-founder Will Olson; not confirmed directly.

Which TikTok, Instagram and YouTube accounts does Vert own or run for Astra and Strum? @getastraapp appears in a Shortimize article about a different 'Astroapp' network, so it is not confirmed as Vert's.
What is Vert's split between paid UA (Meta/TikTok ads, Apple Search Ads) and influencer/organic content? Do they use Superwall or RevenueCat today? Superwall was mentioned in January 2024.
What does '15M+ users' mean: cumulative downloads across both stores, or registered users?

Why are Plug AI's iOS app (no update since 2024-08-02) and Berry (since 2025-02-14) no longer updated: harvest mode, sale or wind-down? The podcast said Plug AI was listed for sale at $3.5M in January 2024.
What does the September 2024 Dribbble job post say verbatim? The page now returns 404, and its figures (4M users, $8M revenue, 8 FTE) come from a search-engine summary.
